description:
P0 REGRESSION from bedrock-q67.21.12 (PR #203, merged 2026-08-24). Every
cluster created before that PR is bricked by upgrading: recovery never
completes and every client read hangs.

REPRODUCED deterministically, variable isolated:
- fresh cluster on develop -> RESULT: nil (works)
- same cluster, same data, system_materializers stripped from the
  bootstrap record -> :bootstrap_names_no_system_materializers, retried
  in a tight loop forever

The user's /tmp/bedrock_00000 decodes to exactly that state:
system_materializers %{}, fresh? false, epoch 3, one log. The record was
last written 13:33 while the worker dirs were touched at 19:25 —
recovery ran and never completed.

TWO DEFECTS, both from the same assumption (a newly added field is
always present):

1. resolve_system_materializer treated "the record names nobody" as
   unrecoverable. The ticket said so outright: "recovery cannot learn
   where the metadata lives, and no retry will change that." That is
   false. The locking phase has already locked every advertised
   materializer and each reports its own shard_id, so tag 0 can be READ
   from evidence. Reading evidence is not inventing a metadata store —
   inventing is what q67.21.12 actually forbids.

2. build_updated_bootstrap used %{record | field: ...}, which RAISES
   badkey for a key the map lacks. A record decoded from a FlatBuffer
   written before the field simply has no such key, so the director
   crashed — on exactly the clusters an upgrade must carry.

FIX:
- legacy path only (field absent or empty) falls back to discovery among
  locked services claiming shard 0; the persistence phase then records
  it and the next recovery resolves by name. One-time, self-healing.
- Map.merge instead of the update operator: adds what is missing,
  overwrites what is not, which is what "rewrite these fields" means.

INVARIANT PRESERVED: a record that DOES name members, none available,
still stalls — even with a healthy stranger locked and available.
Substituting a different worker is the fabrication FDB refuses
(TagPartitionedLogSystem.actor.cpp:2549-2585). Pinned by its own test.

VERIFIED END TO END: the stripped-record cluster now recovers on first
boot, the bootstrap is repaired, and a second boot takes the named path
without discovery. The user's real record bytes rewrite and round-trip
cleanly.

Both fixes mutation-tested independently (restore by re-edit, not git
checkout — sequential checkout restores silently invalidate each other).
title: P0: a bootstrap record predating system_materializers bricks recovery on upgrade
